symptom: All 12 discovered functions of a sectionless ELF64 PIE had size 0, so `kuna functions --min-size 1 --json` answered count 0 / total 12 / error null and `--summary` reported code_bytes 0. 1 instance, round 4 (crackmes.one 605443e333c5d42c3d016f59, KataVM_L1).
diagnosis: funcextent::clip returns 0 when no CODE span contains the entry, and code_spans() is built only from the loader section table. An image with no section table publishes no spans at all, so every entry takes that early return -- 12 of 12 is the only reachable outcome, not a coincidence.
decisions: The filed hypothesis ('segment-only discovery may not propagate recovered extents into inventory metadata') is right, and so is the captain's fix direction: clip against the executable PT_LOAD segments when the section table yields no CODE span. Reproduced independently with the same-binary control -- /bin/true reports 0 of 54 entries at size 0; the same bytes with e_shoff/e_shnum/e_shstrndx zeroed report 11 of 11.

The fallback is whole-table, never per-entry: it triggers only when code_spans(sections) is empty. A per-entry fallback would hand a body to exactly the PE import pointer slots and undefined externals the 0 sentinel exists for, and would make the open `whole-binary-decompilation-treats` need worse.

The gate is 'no CODE span', not 'no sections'. A section table of pure data sections leaves the same empty world an absent one does, and the sentinel is about CODE containment, not about the table's existence.

The loader reports segments as a SEPARATE query (LoadImage::get_segments, a new defaulted trait method) rather than synthesizing sections from segments. Synthesis would have changed function_entries_executable's documented sectionless behaviour ('Loaders without section metadata retain the complete inventory') as a side effect and would have taken the loader lease the five-need sectionless block holds.

ObjectLoadImage keeps the segment metadata in a new segment_info snapshot beside `sections`, not on the byte-owning `Segment` struct: the metadata records each PT_LOAD's whole RAM footprint while `Segment` covers only what the file backs, and the ET_REL path (no program headers) then reports an honest empty list rather than a fabricated flag.

A segment's CODE bit is its execute permission, which lets the same code_spans filter read both vocabularies. Mach-O initprot and COFF characteristics are mapped too; an unmodelled permission word yields no bits, so a reader keying on CODE ignores the segment rather than guessing.
